title: Catheter tip position
view: Anterior view of the neck and upper chest in the radiograph convention: head at the top, the patient's right on the image left.
teachingPoint: A right IJ dialysis catheter runs IJ -> right brachiocephalic -> SVC, and its tip belongs at the cavoatrial junction, not in the atrium. About 13 cm in, inside the record's 12-15 cm.
claims: Anterior view, head at the top, the patient's right on the image left. Skin and chest wall see-through.

The right IJ joins the right subclavian behind the medial clavicle; the right and left brachiocephalic veins join behind the first right costal cartilage to form the SVC, which runs straight down into the right atrium.
The catheter (white) enters at the right IJ puncture (red dot) and follows the IJ, the right brachiocephalic vein and the SVC.
The teal ring is the catheter tip at the cavoatrial junction, not in the atrium.
At true scale (5 px/mm) the in-body catheter length is about 13 cm, inside the record's right IJ depth of 12-15 cm.
Three labels: Superior vena cava, Cavoatrial junction, Right atrium.

geometry.why: the atrium is below the SVC
the SVC lies to the patient's right of the aorta
right IJ is on the image left (radiograph convention)
catheter tip ends at the cavoatrial junction
catheter runs in the right IJ
catheter stays out of the left IJ
